title: Seem Dumber Than Your Mark
summary: Posing as less intelligent or playing the sucker disarms others by making them feel superior and letting their guard down. It eliminates suspicion and makes it easier to deceive overconfident targets, as people naturally gravitate toward those who boost their self-esteem.
example: Prospectors pretended to be foolish and fumbled over a 100,000 dollar offer, setting a smokescreen that eventually allowed them to scam a Rothschild for 700,000 dollars.
Bismarck acted like a foolish and aggressive Prussian, leading his opponent to underestimate him, overlook a treaty, and fall into his trap.
A hunter masquerades as a pig to get close to a tiger, which represents acting dumb to approach a target without raising alarm.
reversal: Showing your true intelligence can help you climb the ladder when dealing with judges rather than competitors, establishing trust and respect.
You can use authority and intellect to cover a deception, such as when Duveen used an authoritative tone and facts to silence a critic claiming an artwork was fake.
